figures.question: What does relaxing cross-incidence sharing mean for the three arms?
figures.caption: Schematic only. A shares every parameter across incident angles; B lets the amplitudes vary per incident-angle group; C additionally lets roughness, anisotropy and Fresnel F0 of all seven lobes vary per group. Attenuation and η stay shared (frozen to A) in B and C.

figures.question: Do the relaxations reduce the error in the mirror core, the shoulder or the tail, and at which incidences?
figures.caption: Region L1 = sum over the region of |model − reference| (luminance, quadrature-weighted) divided by the reference energy in that region. Peak from the independent peak grid.

figures.question: How do the locally fitted lobe parameters change with incident angle compared with the shared fit?
figures.caption: Amplitudes on the common section scale (attenuation knots at their maximal admissible scale), so A, B and C amplitudes are directly comparable. A lobe with negligible amplitude can take any roughness without affecting the response.

figures.question: Do near-duplicate lobes become functionally distinct when parameters are local?
figures.caption: Cosine = per-probe lane-weighted RGB cosine between the angular responses of two terms (WL104H definition). Cosine ignores amplitude, so a pair can overlap even when one term carries almost no energy (see the energy shares).

figures.question: Does relaxing cross-incidence sharing expose reproducible held-out headroom, and is it amplitude or lobe-parameter freedom?
figures.caption: Panels: held-out contrasts, training vs held-out, synthetic controls, transfer, reciprocity, frozen-rule labels.

figures.question: Did every arm converge, and how stable are the starts?
figures.caption: One line per material and start. Wall times were measured while another project's job shared the GPU (contended).

figures.question: Are the new fitting and transfer targets precise enough?
figures.caption: 1024 lanes per probe, 8192 layered walks per lane (depth 1024), fresh direction and walk streams.
